trap-em-dash.evidence: Exactly one spaced dash in the block: 'this is T_{2,3} (trefoil, e^-) — the lowest-crossing operator that unconditionally opens the degree-3 channel.' It introduces a genuine appositive characterisation, and it is the only one in ~40 lines, so there is no density tell.
trap-em-dash.notes: pass. THREE SEPARATE MATH FINDINGS, not fixed inline. (1) q0 PIN CURRENCY: part (iv) quotes 'q_0 = 1.109978595554181... (muon pin, 16 dps)'. That is the OLD muon value; the current CAL-2 muon pin is 1.10997859555733471 (they diverge at the 12th significant digit) and the compute default since the 2026-08-07 owner directive is the proton pin 1.1099785827513808. Proposed: re-pin to proton, or keep muon and correct the digits + label the layer. (2) INVERSE OF A SINGULAR MATRIX: the dual construction states 'on H_n itself det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical', and three sentences later writes K^vee = sum_i c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j with G the 6x6 Gram of H_3(q) — G^{-1} does not exist for the object just declared singular. The construction has to be read on the quotient H_3/rad tr_M = TL_3 the parenthetical names (there the pairing is non-degenerate), i.e. on a 5-dimensional space, not on the 6-element basis {gamma, sigma_0, sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-}. The same formula also has a free index j on the left-hand sum. (3) BRAID WORD: 'the positron (e^+ = sigma_0^{-1} sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0^{-1})' is identified two sentences later with 'the mirror trefoil'. Computed the closure: the underlying permutation of sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_0 in B_3 is the transposition (0 2), which has 2 cycles, so the closure is a 2-COMPONENT LINK (Markov-destabilises to sigma_0^2 in B_2, i.e. the Hopf link), not the 1-component trefoil. The corpus elsewhere fixes e^+ = T_{2,3}^{sigma} at 1 component / 3 crossings (observations/building-block-knots-table1-data.md). Correct 3-strand words for the mirror trefoil are (sigma_0 sigma_1)^{-2} (4 letters) or sigma_0^{-3} in B_2. The same wrong word also appears in mass-theory/breit-wheeler-vertex.md line 34, so this is a 2-block defect.
